title.en: The South-Pointing Needle (Brush Talks from Dream Brook)

edition.en: The entry on the magnetised needle from book 24 of the Mengxi bitan, as given on Chinese Wikisource.
edition.zh: 《梦溪笔谈》卷二十四记磁针的一则，据维基文库。

basis.en: Northern Song prose; the author died in 1095.
basis.zh: 北宋散文，作者卒于 1095 年。

note.en: Shen Kuo's note on the magnetised needle: four ways to mount it, the best being a single silk thread and a speck of wax. It contains the earliest known written observation that a compass needle points not due south but slightly east of it, what is now called magnetic declination. Notice that he ends by admitting he cannot explain it.
note.zh: 沈括关于磁化指南针的笔记：四种放置方法，以独茧缕加芥子大小的蜡悬挂为最好。其中有已知最早的文字记录，指出磁针并不正指南，而是“常微偏东”，即今天所说的磁偏角。留意他最后坦承“莫可原其理”。

excerpt.orig: 方家以磁石磨針鋒，則能指南，然常微偏東，不全南也
excerpt.en: Diviners rub the point of a needle with a lodestone, and then it can point south; but it always inclines slightly to the east and does not point due south.
excerpt.zh: 方家以磁石磨针锋，则能指南，然常微偏东，不全南也
